dedupe_keys.name: entity relationship data model for waste and resource flows in city regions

description: This data model standardises how information on waste and resource management in city-regions is organised, so that data from waste services, industrial symbiosis and urban planning can be exchanged and combined. It was developed by Jonathan Cohen and Jorge Gil at Chalmers University of Technology and published in an open-access journal article. The entity-relationship model defines the components of the system, such as waste generators, collection, facilities, materials, flows and locations, and their relationships, adds circular economy strategies and spatial variables to traditional waste management views, and is translated into a relational database schema. It was checked through semi-structured interviews with government officials, mobile app developers and academics and instantiated for waste management in Buenos Aires, Argentina, and industrial symbiosis in Helsingborg, Sweden. Coverage is generic, with two example cities. The model and schema are described in the article, free to read under a Creative Commons Attribution licence; no separate software download is offered. Caveats: it is a conceptual model, not a populated dataset, and adoption by agencies is not reported. Simulation uses: a common schema for assembling waste flow data as inputs to material flow and waste network models. Related records: the OpenHIE facility registry specification (data-openhie-facility-registry-specification) plays a similar role for health facilities.
